prize_parts.citation: For the discovery and development of halide perovskites as solution-processed semiconductor absorbers for high-efficiency solar cells

statement.case_for: I keep B016 with Miyasaka, Park and Snaith. Round 1 showed that it is the only configuration preferred by more than one member and that Aqvist, Brzezinski and Somfai accept the trio as the natural cut even where they doubt timing. The structural argument has not been weakened by anything said: a corner-sharing ABX3 lattice with a soft, defect-tolerant framework and tunable band gap, explained by crystallography and electronic-structure calculations and reproduced by hundreds of independent groups. The credit chain is short and checkable: Miyasaka's 2009 sensitized cell, Park's 2012 solid-state cell, Snaith's mesosuperstructured and planar architectures showing the perovskite is itself absorber and transporter. I do not claim a majority path exists; I claim this is the one case where scientific substance and attribution are both reasonably settled, and that the chair's question about stability is a question about engineering, not about the discovery.
statement.case_against: The objections from Somfai, Aili, Brzezinski and Chabes are fair. Stability, lead toxicity and module lifetime are unresolved, and a committee can legitimately say a decade is too short. Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis have real claims, and a three-person limit forces an exclusion that some will call arbitrary; Gratzel's dye-cell lineage complicates priority. Somfai is also right that much of the progress is device and materials physics rather than a new bond-forming reaction, so the chemistry framing must rest on the material class and its defect and structural chemistry, and I accept that this is a judgement the committee may reasonably resolve the other way. Finally, the mechanisms of ion migration and phase segregation are still contested by nanoscale characterisation.

responses.point: Somfai doubts the Miyasaka, Park, Snaith cut because Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis all have claims, wants expert reports on priority first, and says the novelty is in materials and devices rather than new bond-forming chemistry.
responses.response: Priority reports are a reasonable condition and I would not object to them. But every three-person cut on this list excludes someone, as your own C-N coupling entry and Aili's lipid entry show; the test is whether the named trio carries the decisive steps, and here the three steps are identifiable and the three most-cited alternatives are mostly refinements (Seok's compositions, Kanatzidis's lead-free and tin variants, Gratzel's later stabilisation work). On chemistry versus physics, I disagree: the discovery that a halide ABX3 semiconductor made from solution tolerates defects and has a tunable gap is a statement about structure and bonding, in the same sense that a new zeolite or MOF family is. The citation should say semiconductor absorbers, not devices, to keep it there.

responses.point: Aili prefers Cullis and Langer for B045, arguing the chemistry is specific (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, endosomal escape, rapid mixing) and the clinical outcome is demonstrated at scale, distinct from the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: This is the strongest maturity case on the list and I take it seriously; I rank it above B016 on demonstrated consequence. My problem is the credit, not the science. By your own account the decisive line is either ionizable lipids with rapid mixing (Cullis, Hope, Madden) or the lipidoid and combinatorial strand (Anderson, Langer), and a Cullis and Langer pair mixes two strands without clearly stating which step is the discovery. Sparr's trio and your pair disagree, and I cannot tell from round 1 which is correct. I would want that resolved in the expert reports before I could vote for it; until then it stays a serious option but not my first choice.

responses.point: Chabes proposes a two-part prize pairing sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry (Balasubramanian, Klenerman) with base editing (Liu), and has moved B043 up as a possible centre of gravity.
responses.response: Thank you for engaging with my seventh ranking of B031. I agree that Liu alone is the right way to credit base editing, but I would not make it half of a prize while it is about a decade old and sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize; your own fallback of B012 standing alone is the more defensible shape. On B043 I share your view that it may become the centre of gravity, but I do not think three names can cover both the PROTAC line (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and the cereblon glue line (Handa, Ito), and the clinical record is not yet in. I would support it later, once degraders have approvals, not this year.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers Gray and Winkler (B062) for protein electron tunneling and notes that opening support was thin and the 1992 Marcus prize overlaps.
responses.response: Your point that low opening support should not end a candidate is right, and I regard Gray and Winkler as rigorous and well attributed. The question I cannot get past is the one you raise yourself: the citation would sit very close to Marcus 1992, and the pathway-model theorists and Dutton are left outside the two names. I would not prefer it to B016, but I would not oppose it as a later prize.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, supports B016 with the same trio and argues the discovery is the absorber and its photophysics, not the module lifetime.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution and with that framing, and I think we should agree among ourselves on citation wording that centres on the material class and not on solar cell efficiency alone, to answer Somfai's concern. I do not share your lower ranking of mesoporous silica as a reason to abandon it entirely; I now treat it as a reserve because the Mobil and FSM-16 priority dispute and the six claimants make a three-person cut contested.

uncertainties: Whether the committee, after weighing stability and lead toxicity, judges B016 early for 2026; I cannot rule out that Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes and Somfai will hold that line.
Whether expert reports would favour including Gratzel, Seok or Kanatzidis in place of one of Miyasaka, Park or Snaith.
Whether B045 attribution can be resolved between the Cullis, Hope, Madden line and the Anderson, Langer line, which would make it a stronger competitor than B016.
Whether B043 can be credited with three names, and whether the clinical record will be sufficient in 2026.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the secretary, Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on B016 or any other candidate I now name. I know the porous-materials community behind B001 professionally but have no stated collaboration with any credited person, and B001 is only an alternative.
